w: Then there's the building. The proposed plan includes about twenty-one billion dollars of capital over four years, about four point four billion of it in twenty twenty-seven. That is close to the four point two billion the City forecasts spending in twenty twenty-six, and about one point eight times its forecast for twenty twenty-five. More than forty per cent of the new capital requests are for water, wastewater and stormwater. Large projects are built by contractors, and the City lists a tight labour market as a risk. Capital that isn't spent is moved to later years. So the question is not only what Calgarians would pay, but what pace the plan would require.

And the growth itself? Half of it was concentrated in just five wards. Those wards have about a third fewer transit stops per person, and seventy-three percent fewer City recreation sites per resident.
